jobs.title: Managing Director, Project Finance
jobs.description:
At Canadian Solar, our vision is to make lives better by bringing electricity powered by the sun to millions of people worldwide. As a leading manufacturer of solar panels, inverters, and energy storage solutions, we've been an industry front-runner since our founding in 2001. Our commitment to sustainability is reflected in all parts of our organization as we navigate the complexities of a booming industry.

Throughout Canadian Solar's subsidiaries, e-Storage, Recurrent Energy, MSS and CSI Solar Co., we invest in our employees' growth. Our training programs and promotional opportunities ensure we all can continue to learn. We understand the importance of work-life balance and provide various flexible work options to support our employees' well-being. Join our team to "Make the Difference" by creating a lasting positive impact on the world and the communities where we operate.

Summary

Recurrent Energy, a subsidiary of Canadian Solar, is seeking a Managing Director of Project Finance to lead the Project Finance department. The role is responsible for providing leadership and expertise to raise tax equity, project debt, and corporate facilities to finance the execution of several GW of solar and storage projects, while also leading project equity sale activities in the U.S

Reporting Relationships & Interactions

Report to the Senior Managing Director of Finance.
Work closely with senior management across Development, EPC, Origination & Structuring, Legal, and Finance.
Provide training and mentorship to Project Finance and M&A team members.
Interact directly with financial institutions and advisors.

Principal Responsibilities / Key Result Areas

Organize and lead a fundraising campaign utilizing banking relationships to raise $2–3B of tax equity and debt over the next three years.
Manage and grow relationships with new and existing financial institution partners. Collaborate with the CFO and Senior Managing Director of Finance to structure and close corporate facilities supporting global financing needs.
Provide oversight and assume overall responsibility for all Project Finance and M&A transactions in North America, including:
Evaluate tax equity and project financing structures to achieve economic and timing goals.
Lead relationships with investors and advisors for structuring, negotiating, and closing project sale transactions.
Guide financial advisors through structuring, negotiating, and closing structured project finance transactions.
Train and develop the Project Finance and M&A team.
Oversee the divestiture of NTP and Pre-NTP renewable projects.
Collaborate with the Business Analytics team to refine development models for anticipated financial structures and tax jurisdictions.
Provide the Business Development team with early-stage evaluations of financing structures and participate in transaction Risk Review.
Collaborate with the Origination & Structuring team on energy off-take strategies, return metrics, and credit reviews.
Collaborate with Legal on structuring Project Finance and M&A transactions.
Evaluate transactions for Investment Committee review.
Partner with Corporate Finance to evaluate accounting, tax, and cash attributes of proposed transactions.
Represent Project Finance and M&A on internal and external cross-functional teams.

Knowledge & Skills

Excellent problem-solving and strategic thinking skills with the ability to provide creative, forward-thinking solutions.
Deep expertise in tax equity and project financing structures for renewable energy projects.
Ability to implement complex financial transactions while balancing tax, accounting, legal, and commercial considerations.

Abilities

Strong team leadership and process management skills with a proven ability to mentor colleagues.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Strong quantitative aptitude with exceptional attention to detail.
Ability to distill complex issues into clear, actionable recommendations.
Highly resourceful and comfortable working in a fast-paced, transaction-driven environment.
Strong sense of ownership, accountability, and attention to detail.

Experience & Education

Bachelor's degree required.
Advanced degree preferred.
18+ years of energy-related transactional finance experience with a strong focus on project finance, structured finance, and tax equity.
Established relationships within the energy and infrastructure financing sector.
Experience working in a project development environment.

jobs.title: Managing Director, Syndications
jobs.description:
Since 1973, East West Bank has served as a pathway to success. With over 110 locations across the U.S. and Asia, we are the premier financial bridge between the East and West. Our teams of experienced, multi-cultural professionals help guide businesses and community members on both sides of the Pacific looking to explore new markets and create new opportunities, and our sustained growth and expertise in industries like real estate, entertainment and media, private equity and venture capital, and high-tech help build sustainable businesses and expand our associates’ potential for career advancement.

Headquartered in California, East West Bank (Nasdaq: EWBC) is a top-performing commercial bank with a strong foundation, an enterprising spirit and a commitment to absolute integrity. East West Bank gives people the confidence to reach further.

East West Bank is committed to delivering customized financial solutions and trusted advisory support to clients across its U.S. and international network. The Bank’s success is built on long-term client relationships, disciplined credit execution, cross-border expertise, and a collaborative culture focused on helping clients grow and succeed.

As part of East West Bank’s continued growth in syndicated finance and capital markets, this role will help expand the Bank’s ability to provide broader financing solutions, deepen lender relationships, and support strategic client opportunities.

The SVP/Managing Director, Syndications will be responsible for leading the origination, structuring, execution, and distribution of syndicated loan transactions across commercial banking, corporate banking, sponsor finance, asset-based lending, and other capital markets opportunities. This individual will partner closely with Relationship Managers, Credit, Treasury, Legal, Operations, and senior leadership to deliver financing solutions that meet client needs while expanding East West Bank’s syndicated lending capabilities.

This role requires a senior professional with deep credit markets expertise, strong lender relationships, and the ability to advise clients and internal stakeholders on capital structure, pricing, market conditions, lender appetite, and execution strategy. The SVP/Managing Director will play a key role in driving revenue growth, optimizing balance sheet utilization, expanding distribution capacity, mentoring junior team members, and strengthening East West Bank’s position as a trusted lead arranger and syndication partner.

This role can be based out of our HQ office in Pasadena, or Orange County, Dallas, NYC or Chicago

Responsibilities

Lead the origination, structuring, underwriting, pricing, syndication, and execution of syndicated credit facilities, including revolvers, term loans, acquisition financings, recapitalizations, refinancings, and other debt capital solutions.
Partner with Relationship Managers and product teams to identify financing opportunities, develop optimal capital structures, and jointly pitch syndicated loan solutions to existing and prospective clients.
Develop and execute syndication strategies that balance client objectives, market appetite, balance sheet utilization, risk management, portfolio diversification, and revenue generation.
Cultivate and maintain strong relationships with banks, institutional investors, private credit funds, alternative lenders, and other distribution partners to expand syndication capacity.
Advise clients and internal stakeholders on market conditions, lender demand, pricing trends, structural considerations, and transaction execution risks.
Oversee the preparation of syndication materials, including term sheets, confidential information memoranda, lender presentations, market updates, allocation recommendations, and transaction summaries.
Lead lender outreach, market soundings, bank meetings, commitment discussions, allocation strategy, negotiation, documentation review, and closing coordination.
Work closely with Credit, Legal, Treasury, Finance, Operations, and Agency teams to ensure transactions are structured, approved, documented, booked, and administered efficiently.
Support the development of syndications strategy, operating procedures, execution standards, lender coverage plans, and scalable infrastructure for a growing capital markets platform.
Represent the firm in lender meetings, client discussions, industry events, and market conversations to enhance the firm’s profile and deepen strategic relationships.

Qualifications

Deep knowledge of syndicated lending, credit structuring, loan underwriting, pricing, documentation, capital markets execution, and lender distribution.
Demonstrated success originating, arranging, structuring, and executing syndicated loan transactions in a commercial banking, corporate banking, investment banking, or capital markets environment.
Established relationships with bank participants, institutional investors, private credit providers, alternative lenders, and other capital providers.
Strong understanding of credit risk, regulatory considerations, loan documentation, agency administration, portfolio management, and bank balance sheet dynamics.
Ability to assess market appetite, advise on transaction strategy, and communicate complex financing structures clearly to clients, lenders, credit partners, and executive leadership.
Strong leadership skills with the ability to manage deal teams, mentor junior professionals, coordinate cross-functional stakeholders, and drive accountability through closing.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare high-quality pitch materials, lender presentations, credit-focused summaries, and executive-level updates.
Commercially minded, detail-oriented, proactive, and comfortable managing multiple complex transactions under time-sensitive conditions.
Experience across one or more lending verticals such as middle market C&I, sponsor finance, asset-based lending, fund finance, entertainment, healthcare, technology, real estate, or other specialty finance sectors is preferred.
Any other duties/projects as assigned

Requirements

Bachelor’s degree in finance, business, accounting, economics, or a related field required; MBA or other advanced degree preferred.
10+ years of relevant experience in loan syndications, leveraged finance, capital markets, corporate banking, commercial banking, investment banking, or related financial services roles.
Prior experience leading syndicated loan transactions and managing lender distribution processes is strongly preferred.
Proficient in Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint, Outlook
Experience with financial modeling, market data platforms, CRM systems, virtual data rooms, and loan agency or portfolio management systems preferred.

Applicants must have legal authorization to work in the United States. We do not offer visa sponsorship at this time.

Compensation:

The base pay range for this position is USD $200,000.00/Yr. - USD $300,000.00/Yr. Exact offers will be determined based on job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and location.

jobs.title: Executive Director, Business Affairs & Legal Affairs
jobs.description:
OVERVIEW OF THE COMPANY

FOX Entertainment With a legacy spanning nearly 40 years, FOX Entertainment is one of the world’s most recognizable media brands and a leading global creator of multi-genre content across broadcast, streaming, digital and emerging platforms. Known for its independent, innovative spirit and bold storytelling, the company is committed to reaching audiences where they are through a platform- and format-agnostic approach to developing, testing and scaling intellectual property worldwide. FOX Entertainment consists of three core business units. The FOX Television Network, which encompasses its flagship linear platform and streaming partnerships with Hulu and FOX One, is home to hit series including The Simpsons, The Masked Singer, Doc, Memory of a Killer, Fear Factor: House of Fear, The Floor and Hell’s Kitchen. FOX Entertainment Studios, operates the in-house scripted and unscripted studios behind series such as Animal Control, Best Medicine, The Faithful, and The Way Home, as well as Bento Box Entertainment with animated hits such as Hazbin Hotel and Krapopolis; Studio Ramsay Global with Next Level Chef, Gordon Ramsay’s Secret Service and Knife Edge: Chasing Michelin Stars; entertainment studio TMZ; and the independent film label Tideline. FOX Entertainment Global is the company’s worldwide content sales and distribution arm. As part of its evolution into a modern next-gen studio, FOX Entertainment is expanding its digital storytelling ecosystem with investments across vertical video with Holywater, Chain’s experiential storytelling, podcasting with Meet Cute, a two-way content pipeline with HarperCollins Publishing, and creator-led formats through the newly formed FOX Creator Studios. Through these strategic initiatives, the company is investing earlier in emerging ideas and new forms of audience engagement, while maintaining the ability to grow successful concepts into premium franchises across broadcast, streaming and global platforms. A prolific content creator and production partner, FOX Entertainment collaborates with leading studios, creators, and platforms worldwide to produce and distribute premium content at scale across broadcast, streaming, and digital ecosystems, while continuing to grow its portfolio of owned IP and next-generation storytelling formats.

JOB DESCRIPTION

Fox Entertainment is seeking an Executive Director, Business & Legal Affairs to lead and support a broad range of strategic dealmaking and legal matters across creator partnerships, production, and emerging technology initiatives. This role will serve as a senior legal and business advisor, partnering closely with business and legal affairs leadership and key stakeholders to structure, negotiate, and execute complex agreements in a rapidly evolving media landscape.

The department sits at the intersection of traditional entertainment, the creator economy, and technology-driven production. The ideal candidate is a highly versatile, business-minded executive who thrives in an entrepreneurial environment within a large media company. This individual combines strong strategic judgment with the ability to independently manage a high volume of complex, day-to-day matters; build trusted relationships with internal and external stakeholders; and develop practical solutions that advance business objectives while appropriately managing risk.

Regular, on-site attendance at the workplace for a minimum of four (4) days per week is an essential function of the position. The selected candidate must be able to reliably meet this requirement.

A SNAPSHOT OF YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES

Support the negotiation, drafting, and execution of a broad range of complex agreements, including creator, production, talent, licensing, content, and technology-related deals
Serve as a legal and business advisor to internal stakeholders, providing practical counsel on deal structure, business strategy, contractual terms, and legal and commercial risk
Partner cross-functionally with production, ad sales, technology, finance, business development, and other teams to structure and execute partnerships and strategic initiatives
Advise on legal, business, and policy considerations arising from emerging technologies, including AI-related initiatives, content creation tools, workflow solutions, and evolving rights issues
Help shape and implement scalable legal processes, contract templates, playbooks, and best practices that support the department’s evolving business needs
Contribute to the development of technology-related policy, guidelines, and governance frameworks as the business models in this space take shape
Navigate a high degree of ambiguity, applying sound judgment to novel legal and business questions where clear precedent doesn't yet exist
Build and maintain strong relationships with creators, producers, agents, attorneys, technology partners, and other external stakeholders
Manage multiple high-priority projects simultaneously while exercising sound judgment in a fast-paced and evolving environment

WHAT YOU WILL NEED

JD degree and active membership in the California Bar; candidates eligible for Registered In-House Counsel status under Rule 9.46 will also be considered.
10+ years of progressively responsible legal experience, including substantial in-house entertainment, media, technology, or related transactional experience; top-tier law firm experience
Significant experience independently negotiating and drafting complex production, talent, creator, licensing, content, and/or technology agreements
Demonstrated ability to advise senior business leaders and influence strategic decisions through practical, commercially minded legal counsel
Strong understanding of entertainment rights, production, talent, and evolving digital media business models
Excellent legal judgment, negotiation, drafting, communication, and interpersonal skills
Proven ability to build credibility and work effectively with senior executives, creative teams, business partners, and external representatives
Ability to lead complex matters from strategy through execution, manage competing priorities, and remain composed under pressure

NICE TO HAVE BUT NOT A DEALBREAKER

Experience advising on AI-related legal, business, rights, and policy issues in media, content, or technology
Experience supporting creator economy, digital media, platform, or technology-enabled production initiatives
Prior experience mentoring or managing attorneys, paralegals, or other legal professionals

We are an equal opportunity employer and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, gender identity, disability, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories consistent with applicable law.

Pursuant to state and local pay disclosure requirements, the pay rate/range for this role, with final offer amount dependent on education, skills, experience, and location is $179,000.00-250,000.00 annually. This role is also eligible for an annual discretionary bonus, various benefits, including medical/dental/vision, insurance, a 401(k) plan, paid time off, and other benefits in accordance with applicable plan documents. Benefits for Union represented employees will be in accordance with the applicable collective bargaining agreement.

jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer, Totalis Speciality Group
jobs.description:
Chief Operating Officer, Totalis Specialty Group

Ready to develop the future of a newly combined specialty underwriting business? Do you thrive at the intersection of strategy, operations and transformation?

If you're an experienced operational leader looking to build, scale and optimise a high-growth business, we'd love to hear from you!

This role can be based in either Eastern or Central US locations, and offers flexibility in line with Aon's Smart Working policy, with the ability to work both virtually and from an Aon office location.

Aon is in the business of better decisions

At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world.

As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

Our Totalis Specialty Group combines specialty underwriting, program administration, distribution, technology and data capabilities to support brokers, carriers and clients, and it’s launch reflects our commitment to creating more connected and scalable solutions across our Risk Capital business.

What The Day Will Look Like

As the North America Totalis Chief Operating Officer, you will play a pivotal leadership role in bringing together Aon's Affinity Programs and MGA business and Totalis Program Underwriters into a unified specialty underwriting and programs platform. Working closely with senior corporate and functional leaders, you will lead the operating strategy. You will also be responsible for transformation initiatives and build scalable foundations to support future growth.

You Will

Develop and implement a multi-year operational strategy aligned to growth, profitability, client experience and risk objectives.
Build, implement and continuously improve the operating model across people, processes, technology and third-party partners.
Partner with business, technology, finance, risk and compliance leaders to drive operational excellence and simplify ways of working.
Lead large-scale transformation, integration and change initiatives, including launch readiness, operating model transitions and technology governance.
Support acquisition integration, new programme launches and future platform expansion opportunities.
Drive performance through governance, service level adoption, automation and operational efficiency initiatives.
Lead all aspects of operational reporting, risk management and control frameworks to support business resilience and regulatory compliance.
Build and develop high-performing teams, crafting an inclusive culture centred on accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement.

How This Opportunity Is Different

This is a rare opportunity to help define the future operating model of a newly combined specialty underwriting and programmes business, at the heart of Aon’s growth ambitions to be the leading insurance advisor.

You'll join at a formative stage, influencing how two complementary businesses come together to create a larger, more connected platform for clients, brokers and carrier partners. You will work directly with senior business leaders and enterprise functions to shape strategy, integration priorities and operational excellence initiatives.

This Role Offers The Opportunity To

Help build a newly combined business from the ground up.
Influence key decisions on governance, technology, service delivery and organisational design.
Lead significant transformation and integration activity with visible executive sponsorship.
Create a scalable operational platform that supports long-term growth across North America and beyond.
Work across a broad collaborator network including business leadership, technology, finance, compliance, risk and operations teams.

Skills And Experience That Will Lead To Success

Significant experience leading operations, transformation, shared services or business execution within a large, sophisticated organisation.
Strong commercial and financial savvy, including experience running budgets, investment priorities and operational performance.
Track record of translating business strategy into scalable operating models and measurable outcomes.
Experience leading large-scale business transformation, integration, process redesign or technology-enabled change programmes.
Exceptional leadership, collaborator management and influencing skills, with the ability to build alignment across senior executive audiences.
Experience leveraging technology, automation, data and AI-enabled capabilities to improve operational efficiency, scalability and business performance.
Experience within the MGA space and digital distribution of insurance programmes to clients, with an understanding of the operational, technology and partner ecosystems that support growth.

Aon is not accepting unsolicited resumes from search firms for this position. If you are a search firm, you will not be compensated in any way for your submission of a candidate, even if Aon hires that candidate.

Nothing in this job description restricts management's right to assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time.

The salary range for this position (intended for U.S. applicants) is $310,000 to $400,000 annually. The actual salary will vary based on applicant’s education, experience, skills, and abilities, as well as internal equity and alignment with market data. The salary may also be adjusted based on applicant’s geographic location.

This position is eligible to participate in one of Aon’s annual incentive plans to receive an annual discretionary bonus in addition to base salary. The amount of any bonus varies and is subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable incentive plan.

Aon offers a comprehensive package of benefits for full-time and regular part-time colleagues, including, but not limited to: a 401(k) savings plan with employer contributions; an employee stock purchase plan; consideration for long-term incentive awards at Aon’s discretion; medical, dental and vision insurance. This role does not accrue vacation. Rather, this role is eligible to take paid time off at the discretion of the employee and management in accordance with company policy and practices. Various other types of leaves of absence; paid sick leave as provided under state and local paid sick leave laws, short-term disability and optional long-term disability, health savings account, health care and dependent care reimbursement accounts, employee and dependent life insurance and supplemental life and AD&D insurance; optional personal insurance policies, adoption assistance, tuition assistance, commuter benefits, and an employee assistance program that includes free counseling sessions. Eligibility for benefits is governed by the applicable plan documents and policies

How We Support Our Colleagues

In addition to our comprehensive benefits package, we encourage an inclusive workforce. Plus, our agile environment allows you to manage your wellbeing and work/life balance, ensuring you can be your best self at Aon. Furthermore, all colleagues enjoy two “Global Wellbeing Days” each year, encouraging you to take time to focus on yourself. We offer a variety of working style solutions for our colleagues as well.

Our continuous learning culture inspires and equips you to learn, share and grow, helping you achieve your fullest potential. As a result, at Aon, you are more connected, more relevant, and more valued.

Aon values an innovative and inclusive workplace where all colleagues feel empowered to be their authentic selves. Aon is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace.

Aon provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment without regard to race, color, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran, marital, domestic partner status, or other legally protected status.

We welcome applications from all and provide individuals with disabilities with reasonable adjustments to participate in the job application, interview process and to perform essential job functions once onboard. jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
We are seeking a Dynamic, hands-on Executive Director to lead critical safety-net organization in south suburbs

Executive Service Corps of Chicago is conducting a search on behalf of Respond Now for an Executive Director role. In this document, you will find details about the role, Respond Now, the responsibilities and requirements for the role as well as compensation, benefits, and where to apply.

Opportunity Overview:

Respond Now stands at a pivotal inflection point in its history. Having scaled to an annual budget of ~$3.8M and a staff of 26 serving over 12,000 individuals across the Chicago Southland, the organization requires a visionary, entrepreneurial Executive Director to transition it from its current operational foundation into a fully modernized, scalable, and resilient institution.

This is explicitly a call for a ‘builder,’ not a caretaker. The next leader will not simply manage steady-state operations, but will actively continue to build the organization's credibility, diversify revenue streams, and inspire its team members to continue to help families in need in the Chicago Southland.. For an executive leader driven by high-impact organizational transformation, this role offers an extraordinary opportunity to stabilize, professionalize, and scale an essential community anchor.

Position: Executive Director
Reports To: Board of Directors
Location: 1439 Emerald Avenue, Chicago Heights, IL 60411 

Respond Now Mission:

Respond Now connects those in need with health, hunger, and housing services in the Chicago Southland. We do this by:
Helping people through their temporary emergencies with financial assistance
Providing food to families and individuals in need
Providing sound referrals and counseling for other needed services

About Respond Now:

Respond Now provides a host of essential services to over 12,000 people in need in south suburban Cook County. Vital services such as food, rent and mortgage assistance, utility assistance, clothing, and transportation are provided to families in over 22 communities in the Chicago Southland. Respond Now is a United Way sponsored agency with funding from private donations, government grants, and corporate and foundation support. It is a recipient of the Greater Chicago Food Depository Quality Performance Award and the Rotary Club of Chicago Heights Paul Harris Community Service Award. Respond Now is an organization with annual funding of $3.8M and 26 staff members.  

For additional information on Respond Now please visit their website here:  https://respondnow.org/

Respond Now is entering an exciting next phase of growth and impact. The Executive Director will serve as a visionary and dynamic leader responsible for advancing the organization’s mission, enhancing the organization's credibility with donors and the board, providing oversight and direction with regards to financial standing, strengthening sustainability, and shaping its future. Reporting to the Board of Directors, the Executive Director will build on a strong foundation of community trust and program excellence while reimagining how the organization grows, engaging donors and partners, and expanding its reach on behalf of families in need in the Chicago Southland.

This is a unique opportunity for a mission-driven leader to make a lasting impact and help guide Respond Now into its next chapter. The Executive Director will provide strategic, operational, and fiscal leadership, ensuring the organization continues to deliver excellent programs for families in need to over 12,000 people in need in south suburban Cook County.

Key responsibilities for this role include (but are not limited to):

Financial Health
- The fundraising function reports to the Executive Director; a key component of this role will involve your involvement in cultivating relationships with corporate, foundation and government funders, and promoting financial transparency and credibility with those funders, as well as the Board of Directors.

The Director of Finance will report directly to you in this role. You will be heavily involved in working with this Director of Finance to oversee financial reporting. Although the Executive Director does not directly prepare these reports, oversight of this function will be a key component of this role.

The Executive Director maintains a personal portfolio of high net worth donors and asks as the ‘face’ of the organization to individual donors, corporate benefactors, government grantors, and state grantors as well. 

Partner with staff managing each segment, such as major gifts, grants, events, corporate sponsorships, planned giving, appeals, crowdfunding, and third party events, to ensure successful achievement of goals.

Programs
- Provide strategic direction to Respond Now’s programs. This will include looking at cost / benefit analyses to evaluate grant opportunities vs costs of programs, analyzing cost-effectiveness of current programming, and analyzing where Respond Now can offer the greatest good to the greatest number of those in need.

Lead the organization through its next phase of development by translating vision into action, aligning programs, operations, and resources with strategic priorities.

Provide inspirational leadership to the Board, donors, staff, volunteers, and stakeholders, fostering a culture of innovation, accountability, collaboration, and positivity.

Organization Mission, Strategy & Leadership
- Serve as an inspirational leader to internal staff members. This will include creating and fostering an environment where team members continue to feel empowered to contribute to the overall growth of Respond Now.  

Partnering with the Board of Directors to establish and evolve the organization’s strategic plan(, ensuring Respond Now fulfills its mission while positioning the organization for long-term growth and sustainability.

Partner closely with the Board of Directors to ensure effective governance, fiduciary oversight, and strategic alignment.

Ensure timely, transparent, and forward-looking communication to support informed decision-making and sustained organizational momentum.

Responsible for leading the staff to operate within the approved budget, ensure maximum resource utilization and maintenance of the organization in a positive financial position.
Ensure Respond Now is in compliance with relevant state and federal laws, regulations and with standard accounting procedures, working with accounting firm and annual auditing firm as needed.

Talent Management -
Oversee employment and administrative policies and procedures for all functions and for the day-to-day operations of Respond Now.

Build a high-performing leadership team and play an active role in attracting, retaining and developing a best-in-class staff. You will have a team of 3 reporting to you in this role.

Ensure new staff members are on-boarded and trained appropriately.

Establish and monitor staff performance and set development goals, assign accountabilities, set objectives and establish priorities with staff members.

Mentor and develop staff using a supportive and collaborative leadership approach.

Requirements:

5+ years of successful leadership experience as an Executive Director with a nonprofit. This is an absolute must have. We will need to see a proven track record working with programs in the human services sector within the nonprofit community.
At least 4+ years of experience in a nonprofit with establishing successful fundraising campaigns (including Federal, State and County grantors, corporate, foundations and wealthy individual donors), and excellent donor relationship management skills.
At least 4+ years of staff management experience to include hiring, performance management, firing skills requiring excellent judgment and creative problem-solving skills such as negotiation and conflict resolution skills.

Since 1973, East West Bank has served as a pathway to success. With over 110 locations across the U.S. and Asia, we are the premier financial bridge between the East and West. Our teams of experienced, multi-cultural professionals help guide businesses and community members on both sides of the Pacific looking to explore new markets and create new opportunities, and our sustained growth and expertise in industries like real estate, entertainment and media, private equity and venture capital, and high-tech help build sustainable businesses and expand our associates’ potential for career advancement.

Headquartered in California, East West Bank (Nasdaq: EWBC) is a top-performing commercial bank with a strong foundation, an enterprising spirit and a commitment to absolute integrity. East West Bank gives people the confidence to reach further.

East West Bank is committed to delivering customized financial solutions and trusted advisory support to clients across its U.S. and international network. The Bank’s success is built on long-term client relationships, disciplined credit execution, cross-border expertise, and a collaborative culture focused on helping clients grow and succeed.

As part of East West Bank’s continued growth in syndicated finance and capital markets, this role will help expand the Bank’s ability to provide broader financing solutions, deepen lender relationships, and support strategic client opportunities.

The SVP/Managing Director, Syndications will be responsible for leading the origination, structuring, execution, and distribution of syndicated loan transactions across commercial banking, corporate banking, sponsor finance, asset-based lending, and other capital markets opportunities. This individual will partner closely with Relationship Managers, Credit, Treasury, Legal, Operations, and senior leadership to deliver financing solutions that meet client needs while expanding East West Bank’s syndicated lending capabilities.

This role requires a senior professional with deep credit markets expertise, strong lender relationships, and the ability to advise clients and internal stakeholders on capital structure, pricing, market conditions, lender appetite, and execution strategy. The SVP/Managing Director will play a key role in driving revenue growth, optimizing balance sheet utilization, expanding distribution capacity, mentoring junior team members, and strengthening East West Bank’s position as a trusted lead arranger and syndication partner.

This role can be based out of our HQ office in Pasadena, or Orange County, Dallas, NYC or Chicago

Responsibilities

Lead the origination, structuring, underwriting, pricing, syndication, and execution of syndicated credit facilities, including revolvers, term loans, acquisition financings, recapitalizations, refinancings, and other debt capital solutions.
Partner with Relationship Managers and product teams to identify financing opportunities, develop optimal capital structures, and jointly pitch syndicated loan solutions to existing and prospective clients.
Develop and execute syndication strategies that balance client objectives, market appetite, balance sheet utilization, risk management, portfolio diversification, and revenue generation.
Cultivate and maintain strong relationships with banks, institutional investors, private credit funds, alternative lenders, and other distribution partners to expand syndication capacity.
Advise clients and internal stakeholders on market conditions, lender demand, pricing trends, structural considerations, and transaction execution risks.
Oversee the preparation of syndication materials, including term sheets, confidential information memoranda, lender presentations, market updates, allocation recommendations, and transaction summaries.
Lead lender outreach, market soundings, bank meetings, commitment discussions, allocation strategy, negotiation, documentation review, and closing coordination.
Work closely with Credit, Legal, Treasury, Finance, Operations, and Agency teams to ensure transactions are structured, approved, documented, booked, and administered efficiently.
Support the development of syndications strategy, operating procedures, execution standards, lender coverage plans, and scalable infrastructure for a growing capital markets platform.
Represent the firm in lender meetings, client discussions, industry events, and market conversations to enhance the firm’s profile and deepen strategic relationships.

Qualifications

Deep knowledge of syndicated lending, credit structuring, loan underwriting, pricing, documentation, capital markets execution, and lender distribution.
Demonstrated success originating, arranging, structuring, and executing syndicated loan transactions in a commercial banking, corporate banking, investment banking, or capital markets environment.
Established relationships with bank participants, institutional investors, private credit providers, alternative lenders, and other capital providers.
Strong understanding of credit risk, regulatory considerations, loan documentation, agency administration, portfolio management, and bank balance sheet dynamics.
Ability to assess market appetite, advise on transaction strategy, and communicate complex financing structures clearly to clients, lenders, credit partners, and executive leadership.
Strong leadership skills with the ability to manage deal teams, mentor junior professionals, coordinate cross-functional stakeholders, and drive accountability through closing.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare high-quality pitch materials, lender presentations, credit-focused summaries, and executive-level updates.
Commercially minded, detail-oriented, proactive, and comfortable managing multiple complex transactions under time-sensitive conditions.
Experience across one or more lending verticals such as middle market C&I, sponsor finance, asset-based lending, fund finance, entertainment, healthcare, technology, real estate, or other specialty finance sectors is preferred.
Any other duties/projects as assigned

Ready to develop the future of a newly combined specialty underwriting business? Do you thrive at the intersection of strategy, operations and transformation?

If you're an experienced operational leader looking to build, scale and optimise a high-growth business, we'd love to hear from you!

This role can be based in either Eastern or Central US locations, and offers flexibility in line with Aon's Smart Working policy, with the ability to work both virtually and from an Aon office location.

Aon is in the business of better decisions

At Aon, we shape decisions for the better to protect and enrich the lives of people around the world.

As an organization, we are united through trust as one inclusive team and we are passionate about helping our colleagues and clients succeed.

Our Totalis Specialty Group combines specialty underwriting, program administration, distribution, technology and data capabilities to support brokers, carriers and clients, and it’s launch reflects our commitment to creating more connected and scalable solutions across our Risk Capital business.

What The Day Will Look Like

As the North America Totalis Chief Operating Officer, you will play a pivotal leadership role in bringing together Aon's Affinity Programs and MGA business and Totalis Program Underwriters into a unified specialty underwriting and programs platform. Working closely with senior corporate and functional leaders, you will lead the operating strategy. You will also be responsible for transformation initiatives and build scalable foundations to support future growth.

You Will

new_jobs.title: Executive Director
new_jobs.description:
We are seeking a Dynamic, hands-on Executive Director to lead critical safety-net organization in south suburbs

Executive Service Corps of Chicago is conducting a search on behalf of Respond Now for an Executive Director role. In this document, you will find details about the role, Respond Now, the responsibilities and requirements for the role as well as compensation, benefits, and where to apply.

Opportunity Overview:

Respond Now stands at a pivotal inflection point in its history. Having scaled to an annual budget of ~$3.8M and a staff of 26 serving over 12,000 individuals across the Chicago Southland, the organization requires a visionary, entrepreneurial Executive Director to transition it from its current operational foundation into a fully modernized, scalable, and resilient institution.

This is explicitly a call for a ‘builder,’ not a caretaker. The next leader will not simply manage steady-state operations, but will actively continue to build the organization's credibility, diversify revenue streams, and inspire its team members to continue to help families in need in the Chicago Southland.. For an executive leader driven by high-impact organizational transformation, this role offers an extraordinary opportunity to stabilize, professionalize, and scale an essential community anchor.

Position: Executive Director
Reports To: Board of Directors
Location: 1439 Emerald Avenue, Chicago Heights, IL 60411 

Respond Now Mission:

Respond Now connects those in need with health, hunger, and housing services in the Chicago Southland. We do this by:
Helping people through their temporary emergencies with financial assistance
Providing food to families and individuals in need
Providing sound referrals and counseling for other needed services

About Respond Now:

Respond Now provides a host of essential services to over 12,000 people in need in south suburban Cook County. Vital services such as food, rent and mortgage assistance, utility assistance, clothing, and transportation are provided to families in over 22 communities in the Chicago Southland. Respond Now is a United Way sponsored agency with funding from private donations, government grants, and corporate and foundation support. It is a recipient of the Greater Chicago Food Depository Quality Performance Award and the Rotary Club of Chicago Heights Paul Harris Community Service Award. Respond Now is an organization with annual funding of $3.8M and 26 staff members.  

For additional information on Respond Now please visit their website here:  https://respondnow.org/

Respond Now is entering an exciting next phase of growth and impact. The Executive Director will serve as a visionary and dynamic leader responsible for advancing the organization’s mission, enhancing the organization's credibility with donors and the board, providing oversight and direction with regards to financial standing, strengthening sustainability, and shaping its future. Reporting to the Board of Directors, the Executive Director will build on a strong foundation of community trust and program excellence while reimagining how the organization grows, engaging donors and partners, and expanding its reach on behalf of families in need in the Chicago Southland.

This is a unique opportunity for a mission-driven leader to make a lasting impact and help guide Respond Now into its next chapter. The Executive Director will provide strategic, operational, and fiscal leadership, ensuring the organization continues to deliver excellent programs for families in need to over 12,000 people in need in south suburban Cook County.

Key responsibilities for this role include (but are not limited to):

Financial Health
- The fundraising function reports to the Executive Director; a key component of this role will involve your involvement in cultivating relationships with corporate, foundation and government funders, and promoting financial transparency and credibility with those funders, as well as the Board of Directors.

The Director of Finance will report directly to you in this role. You will be heavily involved in working with this Director of Finance to oversee financial reporting. Although the Executive Director does not directly prepare these reports, oversight of this function will be a key component of this role.

The Executive Director maintains a personal portfolio of high net worth donors and asks as the ‘face’ of the organization to individual donors, corporate benefactors, government grantors, and state grantors as well. 

Partner with staff managing each segment, such as major gifts, grants, events, corporate sponsorships, planned giving, appeals, crowdfunding, and third party events, to ensure successful achievement of goals.

Programs
- Provide strategic direction to Respond Now’s programs. This will include looking at cost / benefit analyses to evaluate grant opportunities vs costs of programs, analyzing cost-effectiveness of current programming, and analyzing where Respond Now can offer the greatest good to the greatest number of those in need.

Lead the organization through its next phase of development by translating vision into action, aligning programs, operations, and resources with strategic priorities.

Provide inspirational leadership to the Board, donors, staff, volunteers, and stakeholders, fostering a culture of innovation, accountability, collaboration, and positivity.

Organization Mission, Strategy & Leadership
- Serve as an inspirational leader to internal staff members. This will include creating and fostering an environment where team members continue to feel empowered to contribute to the overall growth of Respond Now.  

Partnering with the Board of Directors to establish and evolve the organization’s strategic plan(, ensuring Respond Now fulfills its mission while positioning the organization for long-term growth and sustainability.

Partner closely with the Board of Directors to ensure effective governance, fiduciary oversight, and strategic alignment.

Ensure timely, transparent, and forward-looking communication to support informed decision-making and sustained organizational momentum.

new_jobs.title: AmeriCorps Seniors Program Director
new_jobs.description:
For almost 50 years, Jewish Family Social Agency has been providing care, help and healing to thousands of children, families, adults and seniors regardless of religion, race, ethnicity, gender or age. We are a non-profit, non-sectarian social agency offering counseling services, emergency assistance, a food pantry, senior services, adoptions and professional social services to families and individuals in times of need.
We offer a competitive salary and benefits package, a healthy work-life balance, a collaborative team environment and many opportunities for personal growth and professional development.
The AmeriCorps Seniors Program Director oversees the day-to-day operations, grant management, and volunteer administration of both the Foster Grandparent Program (FGP) and the Senior Companion Program (SCP). This professional role ensures federal compliance, drives volunteer recruitment, and tracks the measurable impacts seniors make in the community.
Program Distinctions
While the administrative duties for the Director are combined, the programs serve distinctly different demographics:
Foster Grandparent Program: Volunteers mentor and tutor children with exceptional or special needs.

· Senior Companion Program: Volunteers provide emotional support, respite, and assistance with daily tasks to frail or homebound adults to help them remain independent.
Program Director’s responsibilities include, but are not limited to:
Grant & Fiscal Management
Administer, direct, and oversee two concurrent federal AmeriCorps Seniors project grants.
Compiling and submitting monthly, quarterly and annual progress reports.
Grant application review and management.
Develop, monitor, and manage program budgets, ensuring all expenses align with federal and local sponsor regulations.
Identify, secure, and document required local matching funds and prepare all required programmatic reports.
Coordinate Advisory Councils for both projects as outlined by AmeriCorps Seniors guidelines.

Compliance & Evaluation
Ensure strict adherence to AmeriCorps Seniors Regulations governing program scope, operations, and grant deliverables.
Track and report performance measurements.
Conduct annual satisfaction surveys to assess the impact of the programs on the community.
Review and analyze outcome data.
Utilize program data to recommend programmatic changes for ongoing improvement.

Supervision of AmeriCorps Staff
Provide day-to-day supervision of the AmeriCorps Program Manager, Case Manager, Data Entry Specialist and Volunteer Coordinator.
Hire, train and evaluate staff to carry out, maintain and improve operations efficiently.
Develop measurable performance goals for each staff member.

Qualifications
Education: Bachelor’s degree in social work, Non-profit Management, Gerontology, or a related field.
Experience: 5+ years of experience in project management, grant administration (Federal Funding preferred), and community volunteer mobilization. Experience working with older adults in a community setting. Prior experience leading diverse teams is required.
Skills: Strong proficiency in budget management, grant reporting, proposal writing, public speaking.
Staff Supervision: 5 +years providing direct supervision to program staff/
Knowledge of adult learning theory, volunteer best practices, social determinants of health and the aging process.

Requirements: Ability to pass a background check and drug screening. Possess reliable transportation and a Nevada Driver’s License. Ability to attend occasional after-hours and weekend meetings/events is required. Regional travel may be required for this position.
Job Type: Full-Time/Exempt
